source_caption:
One of the most sweeping, romantic moments in Pride & Prejudice is the iconic climax where a coatless, sleep-deprived Mr. Darcy emerges from the morning mist at dawn to confess his love to Elizabeth Bennet. However, the filming of this breathtaking scene was decidedly less glamorous due to actor Matthew Macfadyen’s extremely poor eyesight. Macfadyen is heavily nearsighted and obviously couldn’t wear his modern glasses during the take. Because the field was covered in thick, artificial fog and he was walking from quite a distance, he literally could not see Keira Knightley or the camera. To ensure he walked in a straight line and didn’t veer off-course, director Joe Wright had to stand directly behind the camera waving a bright red flag just so Macfadyen had a blurry, colorful target to safely walk toward.

Pride & Prejudice (2005), directed by Joe Wright, starring Keira Knightley, Matthew Macfadyen, Rosamund Pike, Donald Sutherland. A headstrong, independent young woman navigates the intense societal pressures of 19th-century English class and marriage while engaging in a battle of wits and slowly falling in love with a wealthy, socially awkward aristocrat.

source_details.synopsis: Pride & Prejudice is a 2005 period romance film directed by Joe Wright, in his feature directorial debut, based on Jane Austen's 1813 novel of the same name. The film features five sisters from an English family of landed gentry as they deal with issues of marriage, morality, and misconceptions. Keira Knightley stars as Elizabeth Bennet, while Matthew Macfadyen plays Mr Darcy, who falls in love with her. Screenwriter Deborah Moggach initially attempted to make her script as faithful to the novel as possible, writing from Elizabeth's perspective while preserving much of the original dialogue.
